title: Curated: Dubowitz syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 13-year-old Italian male presents with short stature (height 136.5 cm, -2.84 SDS) and delayed pubertal development (Tanner stage I, testicular volume 2 ml). Birth history is significant for intrauterine growth restriction with birth weight 2.470 g (-1.99 SDS), length 45 cm (-2.38 SDS), and head circumference 32 cm (-1.96 SDS) at 38 weeks gestation. Physical examination reveals distinctive dysmorphic facial features including high forehead, epicanthal folds, blepharophimosis, palpebral ptosis, protruding low-set ears with preauricular pits and tags, upturned nose with anteverted nares, and micrognathia. Past medical history includes bilateral cryptorchidism (surgically corrected at 2.5 years), ostium secundum atrial septal defect, unilateral renal agenesis, severe kyphoscoliosis with butterfly vertebra at D2, and chronic eczematous skin lesions. Developmental milestones were significantly delayed with unsupported sitting at 18 months, walking at 31 months, and first words at 18 months, consistent with global developmental delay and intellectual disability. Endocrine evaluation demonstrates growth hormone deficiency (GH peaks 2.02 and 3.16 ng/ml) with bone age delayed by 2 years. Brain MRI reveals hypoplastic anterior pituitary with ectopic posterior pituitary, corpus callosum hypoplasia, and mild lateral ventricular asymmetry.

title: Curated: Ichthyosis follicularis-alopecia-photophobia syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 10-year-old girl presents to the orthopedic clinic with severe progressive limb deformities and functional restriction causing impairment in ambulation. She was born at 36 weeks gestation to non-consanguineous parents with congenital alopecia of the scalp, eyebrows, and eyelashes observed at birth. Physical examination reveals generalized rough, spiny follicular hyperkeratosis with thick plaques and scales, particularly over extensor surfaces of knees and elbows, with lichenification and fissuring. The patient experiences generalized burning sensation of the skin that worsens with increased ambient temperature and requires frequent emollient use to prevent large sheets of skin from peeling off. Complete scalp alopecia is present with sparse eyebrows and eyelashes, without erythema or vesiculation. Musculoskeletal examination demonstrates severe flexion contractures of the knees and equinus deformities of the ankles with resultant fixed flexed posture and inability to walk independently, along with mild elbow contractures and muscle atrophy in both lower limbs. Ophthalmological examination shows mild astigmatism and decreased visual acuity without corneal disease, notably without photophobia. Skin biopsy histopathology reveals orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis, acanthosis, and follicular plugging. Plain radiographs of lower extremities show normal bony structures and joint spaces with contractures attributed to soft tissue fibrosis secondary to chronic skin changes.

title: Curated: MELAS
clinical_vignette: A 65-year-old man presented with a 1-month history of bilateral blurred vision accompanied by dyschrometaphosia and metamorphopsia, followed by diplopia 20 days later. Physical examination revealed a 10-degree outward tilt of the right eye in primary position with preserved extraocular movements, and visual acuity that deteriorated from 0.6/0.6 bilaterally to 0.15 OD/0.1 OS during hospitalization. Visual field testing demonstrated left homonymous hemianopia, while brain MRI showed hyperintense signals in the right temporal cortex on diffusion-weighted imaging. The patient developed progressive cognitive impairment 5 weeks after symptom onset, with MMSE score of 24/30 and MoCA score of 14/30, particularly affecting calculation and visuospatial abilities. Initial EEG at 37 days post-onset showed generalized slow waves predominantly in the delta range, which progressed to periodic triphasic waves at 1.5-2.5 Hz on repeat testing at 6 weeks. Laboratory studies revealed slightly elevated serum lactate levels, while CSF analysis showed elevated IgG synthesis with positive oligoclonal bands but negative autoimmune encephalitis antibodies. PET/CT demonstrated hypometabolism in the right frontal-parietal-temporal-occipital cortex corresponding to the DWI hyperintensity regions. The patient had a medical history of well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypothyroidism.

title: Curated: Floating-Harbor syndrome
clinical_vignette: An 11-year-old female presents with persistent short stature and distinctive facial dysmorphism, having been born at 38 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 2840 g (-0.89 SDS). At presentation, her height was 131.5 cm (-2.59 SDS) and weight was 28.4 kg (-2.0 SDS), despite ongoing recombinant growth hormone therapy initiated at age 4 years when her height was 83.4 cm (-4.63 SDS). Physical examination reveals several distinctive craniofacial features including large ears, a short neck, and a long nose with narrow nasal bridge and wide nostrils, along with mild cubitus valgus and clinodactyly. Her developmental history is significant for delayed language development, requiring speech therapy at age 5 years with ability to speak in sentences achieved at approximately 6 years of age. The patient experienced accelerated bone age progression and early pubertal development at 8-9 years, necessitating GnRH agonist therapy. Previous genetic testing for Noonan syndrome was negative, and chromosomal analysis revealed only a benign inversion p11-q13 in chromosome 9. Blood biochemistry and thyroid function tests are normal, and targeted exome sequencing identified a heterozygous pathogenic variant NM_006662.3: c.7303C>T, p.(Arg2435Ter) in the SRCAP gene.

title: Curated: Peters plus syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 28-week gestational age male fetus presents with severe microcephaly with head circumference measuring greater than 4 standard deviations below the mean for gestational age. Prenatal ultrasound reveals isolated fetal microcephaly without additional structural anomalies detected at the time of imaging. The pregnancy was otherwise uncomplicated with appropriate fetal growth parameters aside from the significantly reduced head circumference. Detailed fetal biometry confirms the isolated nature of the microcephaly with normal limb measurements and no evidence of other congenital malformations on comprehensive anatomical survey. The severity of the microcephaly places this case in the most severe category, with head circumference Z-score of ≤ -4 SD representing profound reduction in cranial growth. Family history is non-contributory with no known consanguinity or previous affected pregnancies. The degree of microcephaly severity suggests a high likelihood of underlying genetic etiology requiring molecular diagnostic evaluation.

title: Curated: Jacobsen syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 16-day-old male neonate, born at 36 weeks gestation via cesarean section due to intrauterine growth restriction with birth weight 2350g (<10th percentile), presented to the NICU with recurrent seizures persisting for over 48 hours. Initial laboratory evaluation revealed severe hypocalcemia (1.2 mmol/L; normal 2.05-2.74), hyperphosphatemia (4.35 mmol/L; normal 1.15-2.15), and hypomagnesemia (0.56 mmol/L; normal 0.7-1.05). Parathyroid hormone level was markedly suppressed at <3.0 pg/mL (normal 10-60 pg/mL), confirming hypoparathyroidism. Despite aggressive treatment with intravenous calcium gluconate, alpha calcidiol, oral calcium carbonate, and magnesium supplementation, the patient required prolonged high-dose parenteral calcium administration via central venous catheter due to persistent hypocalcemia and seizure recurrence when calcium was tapered. The clinical course was further complicated by Pseudomonas sepsis on day 40 of life, requiring two weeks of intravenous meropenem therapy. The patient's hypocalcemia proved refractory to conventional therapy, necessitating initiation of subcutaneous recombinant human parathyroid hormone (teriparatide) at 0.54 µg/kg/24h divided into twice-daily doses on day 58 of life. No dysmorphic features were initially noted, and family history was unremarkable.

title: Curated: Opitz GBBB syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 33-year-old male presents with a 20-year history of exertional dyspnea, chest discomfort, and palpitations, with acute worsening following a recent febrile illness limiting him to walking less than 100 meters. Physical examination reveals signs of congestive heart failure and distinctive craniofacial features including telecanthus and cranial deformity. Electrocardiogram demonstrates sinus tachycardia with frequent premature ventricular contractions (20,412 ventricular beats over 24 hours, representing 20.29% of total cardiac activity). Echocardiography shows severely reduced left ventricular ejection fraction of 28%, atrial septal defect with 0.6 cm diameter and left-to-right shunt, mild pulmonary hypertension (38 mmHg), and enlarged cardiac chambers (LA 4.5 cm, LVEDD 6.7 cm, LVESD 5.8 cm). Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging confirms reduced ejection fraction with increased trabecular muscle mass but no evidence of myocardial fibrosis, delayed enhancement, or perfusion abnormalities. Family history is significant for a younger brother with similar facial features, cleft lip, and congenital heart defects including secundum atrial septal defect and Ebstein's anomaly, while parents have normal facial features and no cardiac disease. Genetic testing reveals a novel X-linked mutation: MID1 gene variant c.875T>C, p.Leu292Pro, with the patient's mother and grandmother identified as obligate carriers.

title: Curated: Dermatomyositis
clinical_vignette: A 45-year-old female presents with a 3-month history of progressive proximal muscle weakness affecting both upper and lower extremities, particularly in the shoulder and pelvic girdle regions. Physical examination reveals characteristic periorbital edema with violaceous discoloration of the eyelids, and erythematous patches over the knuckles and extensor surfaces. The patient reports significant myalgia and a 15-pound unintentional weight loss over the past two months. Laboratory studies demonstrate elevated creatine kinase levels and positive autoantibodies including anti-Jo-1. Electromyography shows abnormal spontaneous activity with fibrillation potentials and positive sharp waves in proximal muscle groups. High-resolution computed tomography of the chest reveals diffuse reticular infiltrations in the lower lobes consistent with early pulmonary fibrosis. The patient has experienced two episodes of respiratory tract infections in the past month and reports mild exertional dyspnea.

title: Curated: Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 4-year-old male presents with severe failure to thrive, having dropped from the 50th percentile at birth to below the 3rd percentile for both height and weight. Physical examination reveals a distinctive facial appearance with micrognathia, retrognathia, and a narrow mouth with thin vermilion borders. The patient demonstrates marked absence of subcutaneous fat with prominent superficial blood vessels visible throughout. Cardiovascular examination is notable for a prominent umbilicus and evidence of early vascular changes. Genitourinary assessment reveals hypoplastic external male genitalia consistent with hypogonadism. Intraoral examination shows a high-arched palate with a shortened lingual frenulum. Audiometric testing confirms bilateral conductive hearing impairment. Laboratory studies demonstrate normal karyotype and routine metabolic panels, though growth hormone levels are within normal limits despite the severe growth retardation.

title: Curated: Monosomy X syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 16-year-old female presents to the endocrinology clinic for evaluation of primary amenorrhea and short stature. Physical examination reveals a height of 142 cm (below 3rd percentile), webbed neck, low posterior hairline, and widely spaced nipples with a broad chest. Cardiovascular examination demonstrates a systolic murmur, and echocardiography reveals bicuspid aortic valve with mild coarctation of the aorta. Laboratory studies show markedly elevated follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) at 89 mIU/mL and luteinizing hormone (LH) at 45 mIU/mL, with undetectable estradiol levels. Pelvic ultrasound demonstrates streak gonads bilaterally with absent ovarian follicles. Bone age radiographs show significant delay, consistent with a 12-year-old skeletal maturity. Audiometry reveals mild sensorineural hearing loss bilaterally. The patient's medical history is significant for intrauterine growth restriction and feeding difficulties in infancy.

title: Curated: Autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 59-year-old male presented with a 2-month history of persistent dry cough and hemoptysis, accompanied by significant weight loss. Physical examination and imaging revealed right hilar enlargement with right middle lobe consolidation and bronchial obstruction, along with a right lower lobe nodule on chest CT. Laboratory studies demonstrated microcytic hypochromic anemia (hemoglobin 84 g/L), thrombocytosis (platelets 430 × 109/L), and elevated inflammatory markers including high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (7.86 mg/L). Tumor markers were significantly elevated with CEA 5.32 ng/mL and CYFRA 21-1 6.24 ng/mL. Bronchoscopy identified a neoplastic mass obstructing the right middle lobe bronchus, which on histopathological examination confirmed adenocarcinoma. The patient had a significant smoking history of 40 pack-years and previous pulmonary tuberculosis. Genetic profiling revealed KRAS p.G13C mutation (VAF: 20.89%) and TP53 mutation (VAF: 12.1%). Staging studies showed no evidence of distant metastatic disease, and thoracic surgery was contraindicated due to poor pulmonary reserve.

title: Curated: Autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2Z
clinical_vignette: A 27-month-old male child presented with a developmental lag of more than one year and progressive fatigue over four months, accompanied by dysphagia and choking episodes during feeding with progressive worsening. Physical examination revealed significant developmental delays and feeding difficulties. Laboratory studies demonstrated elevated serum lactate levels at 5.04 mmol/L (normal <2.0 mmol/L). Electrophysiological examination of motor and sensory nerves showed decreased compound muscle action potential amplitudes, while nerve conduction velocities and latencies remained essentially normal. Head magnetic resonance imaging revealed symmetrical patchy long T1 and long T2 signal abnormalities involving bilateral basal ganglia, thalamus, cerebral peduncles, pons, medulla oblongata, and dentate nuclei. Magnetic resonance spectroscopy demonstrated obviously inverted bimodal lactate peaks consistent with elevated brain lactate. The patient showed no clinical improvement following five days of mitochondrial cocktail therapy including arginine, B vitamins, coenzyme Q10, L-carnitine, and idebenone, and follow-up MRI at one month showed no significant change in the brain lesions.
key_discriminating_features: Abnormality of peripheral somatosensory evoked potentials

title: Curated: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
clinical_vignette: A 49-year-old woman presents with a two-month history of progressive exertional dyspnea and productive cough with whitish sputum that failed to respond to oral cephalosporin therapy. Physical examination reveals oxygen saturation of 90% on room air, bilateral fine crackles predominantly in the lower lung fields, and no other significant findings. Arterial blood gas analysis demonstrates type I hypoxemic respiratory failure with PaO₂ of 58.1 mmHg and PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio of 277 mmHg. Laboratory investigations reveal positive MPO-ANCA at 20.03 RU/mL with perinuclear ANCA positivity at 1:10 titer by indirect immunofluorescence. Notably, anti-GM-CSF antibody testing is positive, and T-lymphocyte subset analysis shows a reduced CD4+/CD8+ ratio of 0.64. Multiple tumor markers are elevated including CYFRA 21-1, neuron-specific enolase, carcinoembryonic antigen, and CA15-3. Complete blood count, inflammatory markers, routine urinalysis, and renal function studies remain within normal limits. The patient denies constitutional symptoms, has no history of tobacco use, and comprehensive evaluation reveals no evidence of active systemic vasculitis at presentation.

title: Curated: Meningioma
clinical_vignette: A 37-year-old female presents with a 6-month history of amenorrhea and headaches, with a significant past medical history of right temporal intracranial mass resection in 1997. Initial laboratory evaluation reveals markedly elevated prolactin levels of 172.9 ng/mL (normal 4.8-23.3 ng/mL), confirmed on repeat testing at 99.6 ng/mL. Sellar MRI demonstrates two distinct pituitary lesions: an 8-mm right-sided mass and a 5-mm left-sided mass. Comprehensive endocrine evaluation shows normal ACTH (37.4 pg/mL), morning cortisol (17.9 μg/dL), TSH (1.895 μIU/mL), free T4 (0.85 ng/dL), and IGF-1 (108 ng/mL). Physical examination reveals BMI of 32.2 kg/m² without acromegalic or cushingoid features. Ophthalmologic assessment demonstrates an incidental left superior quadrant peripheral visual field defect. The patient shows initial response to cabergoline 0.25 mg twice weekly with prolactin normalization to 9.3 ng/mL and resumption of menstrual cycles, but subsequently develops resistance to escalating dopaminergic therapy with prolactin levels rising to 147.8 ng/mL despite increasing doses up to 0.5 mg four times weekly. High-resolution pituitary protocol MRI confirms bilateral sellar masses with persistent hyperprolactinemia refractory to medical management.
key_discriminating_features: Chromosomal breakage induced by ionizing radiation

title: Curated: SLC35A2-CDG
clinical_vignette: A 7-month-old female infant presents with a 3-week history of clustered epileptic spasms occurring in flexion, predominantly upon awakening. The patient was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, but parents report delayed achievement of developmental milestones with loss of previously acquired social smile and visual tracking. Physical examination reveals axial hypotonia with diminished spontaneous movement and poor head control. Neurological assessment demonstrates microcephaly with head circumference below the 3rd percentile, absent visual fixation and following, and generalized hyporeflexia. Electroencephalography shows characteristic hypsarrhythmia with high-amplitude, chaotic slow waves and multifocal spikes during interictal periods. Brain MRI reveals bilateral cerebellar atrophy with delayed myelination and mild cortical atrophy. Laboratory studies including basic metabolic panel, liver function tests, and lactate are within normal limits, while transferrin isoelectric focusing demonstrates an abnormal glycosylation pattern consistent with a type II congenital disorder of glycosylation.

title: Curated: Holoprosencephaly
clinical_vignette: A 29-year-old gravida 2 para 1 woman presents at 18 weeks gestation for genetic counseling following abnormal ultrasound findings. Fetal ultrasound demonstrates severe microcephaly with a single ventricle and absent interhemispheric fissure on cranial imaging. Physical examination of the fetus reveals cyclopia with a single median eye, complete absence of nasal structures, and a proboscis-like appendage superior to the orbital region. Additional craniofacial anomalies include severe hypotelorism and median cleft lip extending through the alveolar ridge. Fetal MRI confirms alobar brain malformation with fusion of cerebral hemispheres and absence of falx cerebri. The patient has no significant family history of congenital anomalies, and her first pregnancy resulted in a phenotypically normal child. Amniocentesis reveals a normal 46,XY karyotype with no detectable chromosomal abnormalities on microarray analysis. The constellation of severe midline facial defects and associated brain malformation represents a spectrum disorder with poor prognosis for postnatal survival.

title: Curated: Oculodentodigital dysplasia
clinical_vignette: A 3-year-old female presents with rapid deterioration of the primary dentition characterized by generalized enamel hypomineralization and subsequent extensive caries formation. Physical examination reveals microcornea, a narrow nasal bridge with underdeveloped nasal alae, and syndactyly of the toes. Digital abnormalities include clinodactyly of the fifth fingers bilaterally. Dental examination demonstrates severe enamel hypoplasia affecting multiple primary teeth with associated pulpal involvement and delayed tooth development patterns. Despite comprehensive restorative management performed under general anesthesia, progressive breakdown of the remaining unrestored enamel occurred within 6 months post-treatment. The patient exhibits characteristic craniofacial dysmorphism with abnormal pinna morphology and broad alveolar ridges. Neurological assessment reveals mild developmental delays consistent with the syndromic presentation.

title: Curated: Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 3-year-old male presents with severe global developmental delay, microcephaly, and failure to thrive since birth. Physical examination reveals characteristic dysmorphic features including micrognathia, a wide nasal bridge with anteverted nares, and a wide mouth. The patient exhibits profound hypotonia and has bilateral cataracts with ptosis noted on ophthalmologic examination. Genitourinary abnormalities include cryptorchidism and hypospadias. Additional ocular findings include retinal vascular malformations and optic nerve demyelination on fundoscopic examination. Laboratory studies demonstrate elevated 7-dehydrocholesterol levels and decreased cholesterol synthesis. The patient has a history of gastroesophageal reflux and malabsorption of fat-soluble vitamins. Genetic testing reveals compound heterozygous mutations in the DHCR7 gene affecting cholesterol biosynthesis.

title: Curated: Autosomal dominant Robinow syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 12-year-old female presents with distinctive craniofacial features and skeletal abnormalities noted since birth. Physical examination reveals sparse, fine-textured hair with slow growth pattern, and characteristic facial dysmorphism including a bulbous nasal tip with tented nares. The patient demonstrates significant brachydactyly affecting both hands and feet. Radiographic imaging shows pathognomonic cone-shaped epiphyses in the phalanges of the hands and feet. Growth parameters indicate marked short stature below the 3rd percentile for age. Orthopedic evaluation reveals bilateral hip dysplasia requiring ongoing monitoring. The patient's hair requires minimal trimming due to its characteristically slow growth rate, and parents report similar features in the father's family history. Laboratory studies including basic metabolic panel and thyroid function tests are within normal limits.

title: Curated: 2p15p16.1 microdeletion syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 4-year-old male presents with global developmental delay, hypotonia, and distinctive dysmorphic features including trigonocephaly and characteristic facial abnormalities. Physical examination reveals significant hypotonia with delayed motor milestones, and the patient has not yet developed verbal communication skills. Dysmorphic features are notable for trigonocephaly, distinctive facial characteristics, and genital abnormalities consistent with his XY karyotype. The patient has a history of neonatal hypoglycemia requiring intervention in the immediate postnatal period. Additional medical problems include chronic constipation, gastroesophageal reflux disease requiring medical management, and vision problems identified on ophthalmologic evaluation. The family reports significant behavioral concerns consistent with autism spectrum disorder, and the patient has been diagnosed with atopic dermatitis. Echocardiogram revealed structural congenital heart disease, and the patient meets criteria for moderate intellectual disability based on developmental testing.

title: Curated: Stickler syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 4-year-old male presents to ophthalmology with bilateral severe myopia and poor binocular vision since infancy. He was born full-term via cesarean section requiring oxygen supplementation at birth. Since birth, he has undergone multiple surgical interventions for micrognathia, cleft palate, and secretory otitis media. Physical examination reveals a flat facial profile, micrognathia, and glossoptosis. Best-corrected visual acuity is 0.12 OD and 0.1 OS with normal intraocular pressures bilaterally. Slit-lamp examination demonstrates bilateral medial upper eyelid entropion with trichiasis causing nasal corneal epithelial roughening, deep anterior chambers, and tessellated fundi with temporal crescents and diffuse macular atrophy (myopic macular degeneration Grade A2). Axial length measurements are markedly elevated at 31.38 mm OD and 32.13 mm OS. Posterior segment OCT reveals bilateral choroidal thinning and atrophy, flattened foveal contours, and thinned neurosensory retina with reduced reflectivity. Corneal topography shows normal thickness (466 μm OD, 456 μm OS) with mild astigmatism. Previous genetic testing reportedly showed no pathogenic variants, and there is no family history of genetic disorders.

title: Curated: DYRK1A-related intellectual disability syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 4-year-old male presents with severe global developmental delay and absent expressive language development. Physical examination reveals microcephaly with head circumference below the 3rd percentile, distinctive craniofacial features including deep-set eyes, and feeding difficulties requiring nutritional support. The patient demonstrates an ataxic gait pattern with significant motor coordination impairments. Behavioral assessment reveals prominent autistic behaviors, including repetitive stereotypical mannerisms and severe anxiety in social situations. The child has a history of febrile seizures and continues to exhibit marked language impairment with no meaningful verbal communication despite intensive speech therapy. Neurological examination confirms moderate to severe intellectual disability with particular deficits in executive functioning. The patient's clinical presentation initially raised suspicion for an underlying neurodevelopmental condition due to the microcephaly and developmental features, but the severity of language impairment and prominent behavioral phenotype suggested a complex multisystem disorder.

title: Curated: Steinert myotonic dystrophy
clinical_vignette: A 15-year-old female presented to the pediatric emergency department with a seven-day history of progressively worsening abdominal pain, particularly in the right quadrants, associated with rebound tenderness and a single episode of low-grade fever (maximum 38.8°C). Physical examination revealed a pale, afebrile patient with generalized abdominal pain but no palpable organomegaly. Laboratory evaluation demonstrated atypical lymphocytes on peripheral blood smear, and immunophenotyping revealed increased TCD4 and TCD8 lymphocytes with CD4/CD8 inversion and NK cell lymphocytosis. Microbiological workup showed positive EBV viral capsid antigen (VCA) IgM with negative VCA early antigen IgG and negative EBNA IgG, consistent with acute primary EBV infection. Abdominal CT scan revealed extensive subcapsular wedge-shaped ischemic arterial splenic infarctions involving more than 50% of the parenchyma. Thrombophilia screening including antiphospholipid antibodies, protein C and S, factor V Leiden, and prothrombin gene mutation was negative, though elevated von Willebrand factor and factor VIII levels were noted. The patient had a medical history significant for primary nocturnal enuresis and was taking desmopressin as daily medication. Electrocardiogram was normal and transthoracic echocardiogram excluded structural heart disease or vegetation.

title: Curated: Cartilage-hair hypoplasia
clinical_vignette: A 19-month-old male presents with severe short stature (height 70 cm, <-3 SD) and failure to thrive since birth, despite normal endocrine function including thyroid, parathyroid, and IGF-1 levels. Physical examination reveals proportionate short limbs, sparse scalp hair, and weight of 9.75 kg, with normal neurological development including independent sitting at 6 months and walking at 13 months. Prenatal ultrasound at 24 weeks gestation demonstrated fetal humeral and femoral shortening, though initial whole-exome sequencing was unremarkable. Laboratory studies including complete blood count, hepatic and renal function, electrolytes, and vitamin D levels are all within normal limits. Radiographic imaging shows characteristic skeletal abnormalities including shortened metacarpals, metaphyseal flaring of the distal radius and ulna with osseous remodeling, bilateral mild coxa vara, widened hip joint spaces, and irregular femoral head contours with heterogeneous density. The patient exhibits normal muscle strength and tone with physiological reflexes present, and notably lacks dysmorphic features such as blue sclerae, high-arched palate, or café-au-lait spots. Family-based whole-exome sequencing identified compound heterozygous variants in RMRP gene (NR_003051.3: n.-21_-9dup and n.5C > T), classified as pathogenic according to ACMG guidelines.

title: Curated: Tay-Sachs disease
clinical_vignette: A 28-year-old male presents with a 3-year history of progressive neurological deterioration following hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Physical examination reveals muscle weakness, progressive spasticity, and gait disturbance with significant skeletal muscle atrophy. The patient demonstrates visual impairment and exhibits atypical behavior with markedly shortened attention span. Neurological assessment shows dysarthria and progressive motor dysfunction. Laboratory analysis reveals elevated serum inflammatory cytokines and abnormal glycolipid metabolism markers. Biochemical studies demonstrate GM2-ganglioside accumulation in tissue samples and abnormal lysosomal enzyme activity. Following adjunctive curcumin therapy, the patient showed a shift in serum cytokine profile toward a less inflammatory state with subjective clinical improvement, though stored ganglioside levels remained largely unchanged.

title: Curated: 22q11.2 deletion syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 4-year-old male presents to the pediatric clinic for evaluation of recurrent upper respiratory tract infections and speech delays. Physical examination reveals a submucous cleft palate with velopharyngeal insufficiency. Craniofacial features include low-set ears with mild conductive hearing loss, epicanthal folds, and telecanthus with upslanted palpebral fissures. The nasal bridge appears wide and prominent with a bulbous nasal tip. Parents report hypernasal speech quality and feeding difficulties during infancy. The child has experienced multiple episodes of otitis media requiring tympanostomy tubes. Laboratory studies show mild hypocalcemia and lymphopenia on complete blood count.

title: Curated: Oculocerebrorenal syndrome of Lowe
clinical_vignette: A 14-month-old male infant presents with bilateral dense congenital cataracts identified shortly after birth, requiring early surgical intervention. Physical examination reveals distinctive ocular findings including irregular pupillary morphology and horizontal nystagmus, with subsequent development of amblyopia despite cataract extraction. The patient demonstrates significant developmental delays with repetitive hand-flapping behaviors and episodes of unexplained irritability and withdrawal. Laboratory studies reveal persistent proteinuria (3+ on dipstick) and elevated serum creatinine (1.8 mg/dL) suggestive of progressive renal insufficiency. Renal biopsy demonstrates abnormal proximal tubular cell morphology with characteristic cytoplasmic inclusions and basement membrane irregularities. Family history is notable for X-linked inheritance pattern, with the maternal grandfather having similar ocular and renal manifestations. The combination of early-onset cataracts, progressive nephropathy, and neurodevelopmental abnormalities suggests an underlying X-linked syndromic disorder affecting multiple organ systems.

title: Curated: Alström syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 16-year-old male presents with severe progressive neuromuscular deterioration and spinal deformity requiring surgical intervention. The patient was born prematurely at 37 weeks with neonatal asphyxia and demonstrated early developmental delays with poor head control and inability to roll over by 7 months of age. At approximately 10 years of age, he developed influenza encephalopathy and subsequently became bedridden. Physical examination reveals severe growth retardation with height of 148 cm and weight of 24 kg, along with fluctuating levels of consciousness and limited communication ability. He demonstrates marked contractures and limited range of motion in all extremities, particularly affecting the left elbow and right knee, with inability to extend the left elbow or elevate the left shoulder. Imaging studies show severe three-dimensional neuromuscular scoliosis with a Cobb angle of 76°, pelvic tilt of 38°, and significant thoracic deformity resulting in reduced lung volume. The patient requires multiple medications including anticonvulsants and various vitamin supplements, suggesting underlying metabolic dysfunction.

title: Curated: Proteus syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 3-year-old male presents with progressive asymmetric enlargement of the left lower extremity and genitalia, first noted at 6 days of age. Physical examination reveals a large erythematous, non-blanching capillary malformation extending from the left thigh to involve the lower limb, buttock, lumbar region, lower abdomen, and bilateral inguinal areas. The left lower limb demonstrates significant asymmetric overgrowth with increased length and circumference compared to the contralateral side. The scrotum and penis show asymmetric enlargement with violaceous and angiokeratoma-like papules present on the skin surface. Doppler ultrasonography demonstrates heterogeneous subcutaneous lesions with multiple cystic spaces showing venous flow, consistent with combined venolymphatic malformation. The patient exhibits thickened, irregular skin texture overlying the affected areas. No audible bruits are detected on auscultation, and peripheral pulses remain normal. Laboratory investigations and computed tomography show no evidence of visceral involvement or systemic abnormalities.

title: Curated: Schwartz-Jampel syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 3-year-old female presents for developmental assessment with a history of prenatal micrognathia and intrauterine growth restriction affecting the limbs. Physical examination reveals distinctive craniofacial features including a narrow oral opening with difficulty achieving full mouth opening, pursed lip configuration, and an everted lower lip with prominent vermillion border. The patient demonstrates full, rounded cheeks and reports visual difficulties requiring ophthalmologic evaluation. Neurological examination shows increased muscle tone throughout all extremities with an abnormal, stiff-appearing gait pattern. Radiographic studies demonstrate irregular metaphyseal bone formation in multiple long bones. Developmental testing indicates mild intellectual impairment with particular delays in cognitive processing. The patient's growth parameters show proportionate short stature with normal weight gain.

title: Curated: Sotos syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 39-week gestational age male neonate, the second child of non-consanguineous Caucasian parents, was delivered via emergency cesarean section due to pathological cardiotocography. Birth parameters included weight 3855g (+1 SDS), length 53cm (+1 SDS), and head circumference 37cm (+1 SDS). Prenatal imaging revealed polyhydramnios, abnormal umbilical and middle cerebral artery flow patterns, and abnormal brain morphology. Apgar scores were 3, 7, and 8 at 1, 5, and 10 minutes respectively. Immediately postpartum, the infant presented with significant hypotonia and severe hypoglycemia (glucose 0.6 mmol/L). The patient required admission to the neonatal intensive care unit for intravenous high-concentration glucose infusions at a utilization rate of 13-14 mg/kg/min. Additionally, tachypnea necessitated respiratory support with continuous positive airway pressure therapy. The combination of prenatal abnormalities, neonatal hypotonia, persistent hypoglycemia, and respiratory distress raised concerns for an underlying genetic syndrome.

title: Curated: Fanconi anemia
clinical_vignette: A 7-year-old Hispanic male presents to the hematology clinic with a 6-month history of progressive fatigue, easy bruising, and recurrent infections. Physical examination reveals short stature (height below 3rd percentile for age), café-au-lait spots distributed across the trunk and extremities, and several hypopigmented patches on the back. Notable dysmorphic features include bilateral absent thumbs and radial aplasia of the right upper extremity. Laboratory studies demonstrate pancytopenia with hemoglobin of 6.2 g/dL, platelet count of 28,000/μL, and absolute neutrophil count of 800/μL. The patient's parents report consanguinity and note that his older sister has similar physical features. Bone marrow biopsy reveals hypocellularity with dysplastic changes in all cell lines.
key_discriminating_features: Abnormality of blood and blood-forming tissues

title: Curated: ZTTK syndrome
clinical_vignette: A one-day-old male neonate was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit presenting with multiple congenital anomalies. The infant was born to nonconsanguineous parents with a history of one prior spontaneous abortion in early pregnancy. Third-trimester ultrasonography had revealed fetal hydrocephalus. Physical examination demonstrated distinctive craniofacial dysmorphism including microcephaly and abnormal facial features. Neuroimaging confirmed significant hydrocephalus with associated brain structural abnormalities. The patient exhibited profound hypotonia and feeding difficulties requiring nasogastric tube support. Developmental assessment revealed severe global developmental delay with absent primitive reflexes. Additional findings included growth restriction and failure to thrive. The constellation of craniofacial anomalies, severe neurodevelopmental impairment, and structural brain malformations suggested an underlying genetic syndrome warranting comprehensive genomic evaluation.

title: Curated: Cornelia de Lange syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 12-year-old female presents with a history of uncontrolled epilepsy, dystonia, and severe behavioral dysregulation. Physical examination reveals microcephaly with brachycephaly, a low anterior hairline, and distinctive facial features including anteverted nares, a long philtrum, and thin vermilion borders of the lips. Additional craniofacial abnormalities include micrognathia, a high-arched palate, and a notably short neck. The patient has experienced chronic breathing difficulties and progressive scoliosis requiring ongoing monitoring. Her medical history is significant for recurrent constipation, previous pancreatitis, and a surgically repaired hiatal hernia. Developmental assessment confirms significant intellectual disability with associated communication impairments.

title: Curated: Pallister-Hall syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 10-year-old child presents to the pediatric clinic for evaluation of multiple congenital anomalies. Physical examination reveals a median cleft lip with associated facial dysmorphic features. The patient demonstrates polydactyly affecting multiple digits. Laryngoscopic examination identifies a rare trifid epiglottis with three distinct divisions of the epiglottic cartilage. The child exhibits developmental delays and growth retardation below the third percentile for age. Additional skeletal abnormalities are noted on physical examination. The patient's medical history is significant for feeding difficulties during infancy and recurrent respiratory infections. The constellation of craniofacial malformations, limb anomalies, and laryngeal structural defects suggests an underlying syndromic condition requiring comprehensive genetic evaluation.

title: Curated: 1p36 deletion syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 3-year-old female presents to the developmental pediatrics clinic for evaluation of global developmental delays and dysmorphic features. The child was born at 38 weeks gestation to a 28-year-old primigravid mother following an uncomplicated pregnancy. Physical examination reveals distinctive craniofacial features including a pointed chin, elongated philtrum, and wide nasal bridge with deeply set eyes. Neurological assessment demonstrates significant hypotonia and delayed motor milestones, with the child unable to walk independently. Speech and language development is markedly delayed, with the patient producing only a few single words at this age. The hands show brachydactyly affecting multiple digits bilaterally. Cognitive assessment suggests moderate intellectual disability with significant delays across all developmental domains. Brain MRI reveals agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated ventricular dilatation.

title: Curated: Leigh syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 14-month-old male infant presents with progressive developmental regression and failure to thrive. The patient was born at term to consanguineous parents and initially appeared normal, but began showing signs of hypotonia and feeding difficulties at 6 months of age. Physical examination reveals marked muscular hypotonia with poor head control and absent deep tendon reflexes. The infant demonstrates abnormal involuntary movements including dystonic posturing of the extremities and intermittent myoclonic jerks. Laboratory studies show persistent lactic acidosis with serum lactate levels of 8.2 mmol/L (normal <2.0) and elevated lactate in cerebrospinal fluid at 6.1 mmol/L (normal <2.2). Urine organic acids reveal significantly elevated lactate and pyruvate excretion. Neuroimaging demonstrates bilateral symmetric hyperintense lesions in the basal ganglia and brainstem on T2-weighted MRI sequences. The patient has experienced recurrent episodes of metabolic decompensation requiring hospitalization for correction of severe acidosis.

title: Curated: Wolf-Hirschhorn syndrome
clinical_vignette: A 4-year-old female presents to the pediatric neurology clinic with a history of intrauterine growth retardation and decreased fetal movement noted during pregnancy. Physical examination reveals distinctive craniofacial features including downslanted palpebral fissures and frontal bossing. The patient demonstrates significant hypotonia and ataxic gait pattern. Neurological assessment confirms global developmental delay with absence of verbal communication and persistent failure to thrive since birth. The patient has experienced multiple seizure episodes requiring anticonvulsant therapy. Dental examination reveals hypodontia with several missing primary teeth. Growth parameters remain consistently below the 3rd percentile for age despite nutritional interventions.
